technology.summary: Today's most important technology news includes Microsoft's decision to allow Microsoft 365 Family and Premium subscribers to share AI benefits, as well as the company's dispute with the US over alleged immigration rule abuse. OpenAI is standing firm on its decision to fire three AI safety researchers, while Meta has banned ads from TikTok's parent company ByteDance across the US and several other countries. Google's new operating system, Googlebook, has received mixed reviews, with praise for its hardware but criticism of its software. Meanwhile, Instinct, an AI agent startup, has gained buzz for its text message-based interface. TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 is also underway, featuring various networking events and startup showcases in San Francisco.

finance.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India and the Reserve Bank of India have joined forces to streamline regulatory procedures and facilitate the entry of foreign portfolio investors into the market. This comes amid a challenging market landscape characterized by high crude oil prices, rising bond yields, and persistent foreign selling. In other news, a resurgent El Niño pattern may exacerbate the selloff in Southeast Asian bonds, potentially driving up yields as US Treasury rates and oil prices rise. Meanwhile, Indian hospital stocks have taken a hit following a Supreme Court ruling on steep cancer drug markups, with the BSE Hospitals Index dropping 5%.

politics.summary: Today's most important politics news includes the Delhi High Court's dismissal of pleas for a SIT probe into the 2020 riots and 2019 Jamia violence. The Supreme Court will list a plea to allow peaceful protests at Jantar Mantar, where protesters are demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Congress has condemned the detention of tribal students headed for a protest in Mumbai, while Jairam Ramesh has attacked the CEC for executing illegal orders. Former US President Donald Trump has called the US electoral process 'corrupt', citing a non-existent Indian election. India's foreign exchange reserves have reportedly declined by $18.34 billion in a single week, and Bengali actor Koel Mallick has joined the BJP.
